summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue fell 22% YoY to about INR 507 crore and H1 EBITDA was about INR 106 crore, with management guiding FY27 revenue flat to down.
summary.overview: Dishman Carbogen Amcis reported a soft Q2 FY27 with revenue of about INR 507 crore, down 22% YoY, driven by lower development revenue, weaker Vitamin D analogs (Calcifediol and Calcitriol) and lower drug product sales. Quarterly EBITDA was about INR 46 crore and H1 EBITDA about INR 106 crore, with CDMO margins falling sharply to 12.3% in Q2 from 25%. Management attributed the weakness to deferred shipments and biotech customers delaying work due to funding constraints, and said FY27 revenue will not grow. It pointed to early-phase order recovery, technology transfers from Switzerland to Bavla, and an ECB whose first drawdown (about EUR/CHF 50 million per the call) is expected before year-end to cut interest costs.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR 388 crore vs INR 509 crore last year; H1 INR 929 crore vs INR 1,120 crore. Segment margin 12.3% in Q2 (vs 25%) and 8.7% in H1 (vs 21%).

segments.name: Marketable Molecules
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 118 crore vs INR 143 crore; H1 INR 256 crore vs INR 240 crore. Lower margins from Vitamin D analogs decline; management expects a stronger H2 uplift in Vitamin D analogs, the most profitable sub-segment.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue not expected to grow over FY26 (about INR 2,900 crore); management aims to get closer to that number by year-end.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at about 15-16% (given earlier on the call); management declined to give an absolute FY27 operating profit (analyst's INR 500 crore estimate not confirmed).
Medium term: at least high-single-digit to double-digit top-line growth; FY28-29 top-line growth of at least 10-12% per year and EBITDA margin above 20-21%.
Bavla expected to deliver above INR 400-450 crore revenue in FY28 as technology transfers complete; a quarterly run rate of INR 150 crore timing not committed.

ECB: first drawdown targeted before Christmas, otherwise January or Q4 FY27; quarterly interest cost expected to fall to about INR 20-25 crore from about INR 40 crore (annual saving about INR 80-85 crore).
FY27 capex guided at about INR 200 crore including maintenance and SAP digital transformation; Q2 capex about USD 5.4 million, H1 about USD 10.3 million.
capex_capacity: Bavla: last large capex completed, including the largest BWT Switzerland water purification system in India, positioned as the base for future capacity expansion and restart of idle plants.
Bavla and Naroda: rising audits and RFPs following FDA and NDA approvals; Naroda secured first commercial contract after July 2026 product approval for a macrocyclic peptide.

Technology transfers: first commercial legacy transfer from Carbogen Amcis (American customer) on schedule for completion by FY-end; validation batches expected around March-April 2027; about three commercial, two intermediate and KSM transfers in the pipeline.
Japanese innovator molecule co-investment expansion on track; second co-investment expected to go live in FY28, adding capacity.
Drug product (soft gel): a customer with a commercial product is evaluating a co-investment to add capacity; late-phase quotations outstanding.
demand_pricing: Early-phase enquiries are picking up as biotech funding returns, with the early-phase development pipeline rising to about CHF 98 million from about CHF 89 million in Q1.
Late-phase portfolio above 12 projects including PPQ campaigns; late-phase molecules rose from 10 to about 13 in six months; one molecule commercialised.
Customers requested a quotation for an initial volume of several hundred metric tonnes for a semiconductor-related project.
Increased order income from existing commercial products as customers restock after pandemic-era destocking.
Management says Swiss pricing is a disadvantage in small-scale biotech work, so India-based volume manufacturing is being pitched to big pharma.
Vitamin D analogs (Calcifediol) sales carry high margins; US sales team expanded and South American orders won; Halal certification planned for Veenendaal.

qa_highlights.question: Why are small Indian pharma firms winning large single-molecule CDMO contracts while Bavla has not secured one?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business is lumpy and targets big pharma Phase III molecules for commercial manufacturing in India; tech transfers take time because customers must update regulatory filings.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 keep high-single-digit growth guidance, and when will Bavla reach INR 150 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 may show no top-line growth because deferred orders moved to next year; Bavla could reach above INR 400-450 crore in FY28, with no firm quarter given.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and size of ECB and interest cost reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: First drawdown of about 50 million (currency as stated on call) targeted before Christmas, else January or Q4; quarterly interest to fall to INR 20-25 crore from about INR 40 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 revenue drop so sharply and was it anticipated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said August-September development revenue was below plan as some orders slipped into FY28 due to customer funding constraints; no shock but a surprise versus last quarter's tone.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a dependency on funding for the ECB and why has the timeline slipped?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays were attributed to holiday-season slowdowns, share transfers and family settlement steps, multi-jurisdiction law firms and banks; the company expects completion in the current month.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA outlook for FY28 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY28-29 top-line growth of at least 10-12% a year and EBITDA margin above 20-21%, contingent on how FY27 closes.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness: customer-driven timing of development and tech transfer milestones; Q2 shows deferral risk could recur.
Biotech funding dependence: management says funds were diverted to AI companies; early-phase recovery is not yet visible in revenue.
Margin pressure from fixed costs (employee expenses about INR 321 crore a quarter) with revenue falling; CDMO margin fell to 12.3%.
ECB and fundraise execution: multiple conditions precedent and tax opinions outstanding; slippage to January 2027 flagged as worst case.
Vitamin D analogs recovery in H2 is needed to lift Marketable Molecules margins; the mix shift toward cholesterol business weighed on H1.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term numbers, acknowledging a soft quarter and deferred orders, but confident and optimistic on the medium term. Several answers were long and indirect, and pressed analysts on timelines (ECB, Bavla ramp) that repeatedly slipped, which drew pushback from analysts on credibility.

since most of our expenses are fixed in nature, the decline in the revenue would have a significant impact on the EBITDA.
it's not that the orders have been lost, it is something which we might need to service in the next financial year

adds.what: Japanese innovator molecule co-investment expansion (second co-investment)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided flat to no growth over about INR 2,900 crore (a cut), with FY28 Bavla revenue of INR 400-450 crore and 10-12% medium-term growth; delivery rests on early-phase order recovery, Bavla tech transfers and Vitamin D analogs, with few specific capacity numbers or contracts beyond a first Naroda commercial contract.

oneOffs.what: Deferred shipments and customer-timing slippage: August-September development revenue below plan as some orders moved into FY28; revenue is deferred, not added

quality.why: Q2 revenue fell 22% YoY to about INR 507 crore, with CDMO down to INR 388 crore from INR 509 crore and management citing deferred orders and biotech funding delays rather than a recurring base, so the decline is mostly timing-driven and FY27 is guided flat to down.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 15-16% versus CDMO margin falling to 12.3% in Q2 from 25%, with revenue down 22% YoY and employee costs about INR 321 crore a quarter; margin lift depends on Vitamin D analog recovery in H2 and ECB interest savings of about INR 80-85 crore a year.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bavla expected to deliver INR 400-450 crore revenue in FY28 as tech transfers complete (first legacy validation batches Mar-Apr 2027), and second Japanese co-investment goes live in FY28, but no firm capacity numbers beyond that.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to no growth over about INR 2,900 crore after H1 of INR 1,185 crore (about -13% YoY), with deferred orders slipping into FY28; growth only resumes in FY28-29 at 10-12% a year.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex held at about INR 200 crore (H1 about USD 10.3 million) and a drug product customer is evaluating a co-investment to add capacity, but no new capex is firmly announced and utilisation is not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was cut to no growth over FY26 (about INR 2,900 crore) and FY27 EBITDA margin is guided at 15-16%, with management saying deferred orders could push into FY28.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue lumpiness and biotech funding dependence (early-phase pipeline rose to CHF 98 million from CHF 89 million but not yet in revenue) leave FY27 flat-to-down risk, and ECB slippage to January 2027 is flagged as worst case.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First Naroda commercial contract for a macrocyclic peptide after July 2026 approval and about three commercial, two intermediate and KSM tech transfers in the pipeline, but no named launch dates or revenue sizes.

rows.label: ECB first drawdown cuts quarterly interest to INR 20-25 crore
rows.why: Quarterly interest expected to fall from about INR 40 crore to INR 20-25 crore (annual saving about INR 80-85 crore), but first drawdown has already slipped repeatedly and could move to January 2027.

rows.label: Early-phase biotech pipeline recovery
rows.why: Early-phase development pipeline rose to about CHF 98 million from CHF 89 million in Q1 and late-phase molecules rose from 10 to about 13 in six months, but early-phase recovery is not yet visible in revenue.

rows.label: Semiconductor-related bulk quotation
rows.why: Customers requested a quotation for an initial volume of several hundred metric tonnes, but no order has been won and the call gave no size or timing.

tone.note: Management was cautious on near-term numbers (Q2 revenue down 22%, FY27 flat, EBITDA margin 15-16%) but confident on the medium term (10-12% growth, 20-21% margin in FY28-29); analysts pushed on the repeatedly slipped ECB and Bavla ramp timelines and the credibility of the FY28 targets.
